newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND BANK'S VANHALA SEES NO RATE TRAPS IN ERM.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND BANK'S VANHALA SEES NO RATE TRAPS IN ERM.

text.p: Bank of Finland board member Matti Vanhala said on Thursday that the wide 15 percent fluctuation bands in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) would put no pressure on Finnish interest rates.
"In this new ERM, there is no risk to fall into repeated interest rate traps, that is to be forced into defensive interest rate policy actions following tight fluctuation bands," he said.

The markka joined the ERM on October 14 at a central rate of 3.04 to the German mark and is allowed to fluctuate by up to 15 percent against all currencies in the grid, which is much more than the old 2.5 percent fluctuation range the ERM would have allowed, he noted.
The ERM fluctuation bands were widened in August 1993 after severe pressure on the system.

Vanhala repeated an earlier view that German interest rates should not be seen a bottom for Finnish rates, controlled by the Bank of Finland's one-month tender rate which is currently the same as the German 14-day repo rate -- 3.00 percent.
"We should not think that German mark interest rates are the floor ... all depends on our own fiscal policy and economic prospects, he said.
"If (prospects) remain strong, our interest rates will be fairly satisfactory," he said.
